meta.title: Development Law Docket
meta.what_this_is: Indian court judgments that changed what development organisations, state programmes and rights-holders can actually do.
meta.what_this_is_not: Legal advice. Holdings are summarised editorially; the linked judgment is authoritative. Case law changes — check the status field and the date.
meta.verification: Every entry's case name and decision year were checked against the judgment text, and each entry lists the specific terms confirmed present in that text. Summaries of what a case means are editorial and were not separately adjudicated.

excluded.case: PUCL v. Union of India (right to food)
excluded.why: Resolved to a single 2007 interim order that does not carry the terms the summary claimed. The case is a continuing mandamus with many orders; it needs per-order entries rather than one.

excluded.case: Sampurna Behura v. Union of India
excluded.why: Resolved to a short order lacking the claimed terms; needs the substantive judgment.
Search did not resolve it to a document that passed the name-and-year check.

excluded.case: Devika Biswas v. Union of India (2016)
Society for Unaided Private Schools v. Union of India (2012)
Consumer Education & Research Centre v. Union of India (1995)
excluded.why: Search matched LIC v. CERC, a different case. Excluded rather than shipped on a false match.

judgments.case: Aureliano Fernandes vs State Of Goa . on 12 May, 2023
judgments.holding: Found serious gaps in POSH implementation across public and private institutions and directed verification that Internal Committees actually exist and function.
judgments.what_changed: Put institutions on notice that a committee whose members and procedure cannot be evidenced is treated as no committee at all. Directly relevant to NGOs relying on a nominal ICC.

judgments.case: Deepika Singh vs Central Administrative Tribunal on 16 August, 2022
judgments.holding: Atypical families — including single-parent, queer and reconstituted households — are entitled to equal protection of benefits like maternity leave.
judgments.what_changed: Widens 'family' in benefit administration, relevant to HR policy and to programme eligibility criteria that assume a nuclear household.

judgments.case: Noel Harper vs Union Of India on 8 April, 2022
judgments.holding: Upheld the 2020 FCRA amendments, including the bar on transferring foreign contribution to other organisations and mandatory SBI New Delhi account opening.
judgments.what_changed: Ends the sub-granting model. An organisation receiving foreign funds cannot pass them to a partner, which reshapes how intermediary and consortium funding is structured in India.

judgments.case: X vs The Principal Secretary Health And ... on 29 September, 2022
judgments.holding: Unmarried women are entitled to termination up to 24 weeks on the same terms as married women; 'husband' in the MTP Rules is read as 'partner'.
judgments.what_changed: Removed marital status as a gate on abortion access, and recognised marital rape for the limited purpose of the MTP Act.

judgments.case: The State Of Kerala vs Leesamma Joseph on 28 June, 2021
judgments.holding: Reservation for persons with disabilities applies to promotion, not only to entry-level recruitment.
judgments.what_changed: Closed the loophole by which disabled employees were recruited under quota and then held at the same grade for a career.

judgments.case: Vikash Kumar vs Union Public Service Commission on 11 February, 2021
judgments.holding: Reasonable accommodation is a substantive right, not a concession; denying a scribe to a candidate with writer's cramp because he fell outside the benchmark-disability category was discriminatory.
judgments.what_changed: Broke the assumption that RPwD entitlements begin only at 40% benchmark disability. Accommodation is owed on the basis of need, which changes exam, workplace and service-delivery practice.

judgments.case: Alembic Pharmaceuticals Ltd. vs Rohit Prajapati . on 1 April, 2020
judgments.holding: Ex post facto environmental clearance is contrary to law; a project cannot regularise construction already carried out without clearance.
judgments.what_changed: Removes the 'build first, regularise later' route that had become routine, and is the citation for challenging retrospective clearances.

judgments.case: Secr.,Ministry Of Defence vs Babita Puniya on 17 February, 2020
judgments.holding: Directed grant of permanent commission to women officers in the Army, rejecting arguments from physiological differences and troop attitudes.
judgments.what_changed: Named stereotype-based justification as discrimination — reasoning that transfers directly to any employer defending exclusion on grounds of 'suitability'.

judgments.case: Indian Social Action Forum(Insaf) vs Union Of India on 6 March, 2020
judgments.holding: Read down the 'organisation of a political nature' provisions so that ordinary advocacy and rights work does not, by itself, disqualify an organisation from foreign funding.
judgments.what_changed: Protects issue-based campaigning from being classed as political activity — the distinction most likely to be argued in an FCRA proceeding against an NGO.

judgments.case: In Re Problems And Miseries Of Migrant ... vs In The Supreme Court Of India on 26 May, 2020
judgments.holding: In suo motu proceedings during the COVID-19 lockdown, directed transport, dry rations and registration for stranded migrant workers.
judgments.what_changed: Produced the direction to build a national database of unorganised workers, and stands as the record of what the absence of one cost.

judgments.case: Hanuman Laxman Aroskar vs Union Of India on 29 March, 2019
judgments.holding: Suspended an airport's environmental clearance for non-disclosure and inadequate appraisal, holding that the EIA process must be substantively, not formally, complied with.
judgments.what_changed: Establishes that an incomplete or misleading EIA is a ground to set clearance aside — the practical basis for scrutinising project disclosures.

judgments.case: Cen.Pub.Information Officer,Sci . vs Subhash Chandra Agarwal on 13 November, 2019
judgments.holding: The office of the Chief Justice of India is a public authority under the RTI Act; judicial independence is not a blanket exemption from disclosure.
judgments.what_changed: Removed the argument that a constitutional office sits outside the RTI Act, while keeping a public-interest balancing test for personal information.

judgments.case: Common Cause (A Regd. Society) vs Union Of India on 9 March, 2018
judgments.holding: Recognised the right to die with dignity, permitting passive euthanasia and advance directives with procedural safeguards.
judgments.what_changed: Established the living will in India and made withdrawal of life support lawful under a defined procedure.
judgments.status_note: A Constitution Bench simplified the advance-directive procedure in 2023 after the original safeguards proved unworkable in practice. Follow the revised procedure, not the 2018 one.

judgments.case: Joseph Shine vs Union Of India on 27 September, 2018
judgments.holding: Struck down adultery as a criminal offence, holding it treated a wife as her husband's property.
judgments.what_changed: Cited well beyond adultery, for the proposition that laws resting on a woman's subordinate status fail Article 14.

judgments.case: Navtej Singh Johar vs Union Of India Ministry Of Law And ... on 6 September, 2018
judgments.holding: Section 377 IPC is unconstitutional insofar as it criminalises consensual sexual acts between adults.
judgments.what_changed: Decriminalisation removed the threat that made outreach to LGBTQ+ communities legally hazardous, and reframed programme design around dignity rather than risk.

judgments.case: Justice K.S.Puttaswamy(Retd) vs Union Of India on 26 September, 2018
judgments.holding: Upheld Aadhaar for subsidies and welfare under Section 7, struck down mandatory linking by private entities and Section 57.
judgments.what_changed: Limits when Aadhaar may be demanded. A private organisation cannot require it, and exclusion caused by authentication failure remains a live ground of challenge.

judgments.case: Disabled Right Group vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2017
judgments.holding: Directed enforcement of the statutory reservation for persons with disabilities in higher education institutions, including centrally funded ones.
judgments.what_changed: Gave disability-rights organisations an enforceable handle on institutions that had treated the education quota as optional.

judgments.case: Independent Thought vs Union Of India on 11 October, 2017
judgments.holding: Read down the exception permitting marital intercourse with a wife aged 15 to 18, making it rape.
judgments.what_changed: Removed the contradiction under which a girl was protected by POCSO and unprotected by the marital exception. Practically important for child-marriage casework.

judgments.case: Justice K.S.Puttaswamy(Retd) And Anr. vs Union Of India And Ors. on 24 August, 2017
judgments.holding: A nine-judge bench held privacy is a fundamental right intrinsic to Article 21, and set a proportionality test for any intrusion.
judgments.what_changed: Every data-collection decision in Indian development work now sits under a proportionality test: legality, necessity, proportionality, procedural safeguards. The foundation of the DPDP Act.

judgments.case: Rajive Raturi vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2017
judgments.holding: Directed Union and State governments to make public buildings, transport and information accessible within fixed timelines under the RPwD Act.
judgments.what_changed: Converted accessibility from an aspiration in the Act into a supervised programme with deadlines, and gave organisations a citation for demanding accessible premises and formats.

judgments.case: Shayara Bano vs Union Of India And Ors. Ministry Of Women ... on 22 August, 2017
judgments.holding: Set aside instant triple talaq as arbitrary and not protected as an essential religious practice.
judgments.what_changed: Removed unilateral instant divorce, changing the legal position for Muslim women in maintenance and matrimonial casework.
judgments.status_note: Followed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, which criminalised the pronouncement. The statute, and the debate over criminalisation, now govern practice.

judgments.case: Jeeja Ghosh vs Union Of India on 12 May, 2016
judgments.holding: Offloading a passenger with cerebral palsy without assessment violated her dignity; the Court awarded compensation and stressed the social model of disability.
judgments.what_changed: Made dignity, not medical fitness, the test for excluding a disabled person from a service — with damages attached, which is what gets service providers to change protocol.

judgments.case: Swaraj Abhiyan vs Union Of India And Ors on 13 May, 2016
judgments.holding: Directed States to declare drought where conditions warranted and to implement NFSA and MGNREGA entitlements during it.
judgments.what_changed: Established that a State cannot avoid relief obligations by not declaring a drought — useful wherever a declaration is being withheld.

judgments.case: Laxmi vs Union Of India & Ors on 10 April, 2015
judgments.holding: Directed regulation of acid sales, compensation for survivors, and treatment obligations on hospitals.
judgments.what_changed: Created a concrete compensation and treatment entitlement, and made retail regulation a supervised obligation on States.
judgments.status_note: Relief was issued across several orders between 2013 and 2015 rather than in one judgment; cite the order relied on.

judgments.case: Reserve Bank Of India vs Jayantilal N. Mistry on 16 December, 2015
judgments.holding: A regulator cannot claim a fiduciary relationship with the entities it regulates to withhold inspection reports from the public.
judgments.what_changed: Strong authority against 'fiduciary capacity' refusals, which regulators and public bodies use routinely to deny disclosure about the institutions they oversee.

judgments.case: Shreya Singhal vs U.O.I on 24 March, 2015
judgments.holding: Struck down Section 66A of the IT Act as vague and overbroad, and read down intermediary takedown obligations.
judgments.what_changed: The governing authority on online speech, and on the limits of takedown demands against platforms.
judgments.status_note: Section 66A continues to be invoked by police years after being struck down — the Supreme Court has repeatedly had to reiterate that it is void. A charge under it is not merely wrong but a nullity.

judgments.case: Lalita Kumari vs Govt.Of U.P.& Ors on 12 November, 2013
judgments.holding: Registration of an FIR is mandatory where information discloses a cognizable offence; a preliminary inquiry is permitted only in limited categories.
judgments.what_changed: The citation used when a police station refuses to register a complaint — the single most common obstacle in frontline rights casework.

judgments.case: Orissa Mining Corporation Ltd vs Ministry Of Environment & Forest &Ors on 18 April, 2013
judgments.holding: Referred the question of religious and cultural rights over the Niyamgiri hills to the Gram Sabhas, whose decision would bind the clearance process.
judgments.what_changed: The strongest Indian authority for community consent over a project. Turned Forest Rights Act consultation into a decision the Gram Sabha actually makes.

judgments.case: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande vs Cen.Information Commr.& Ors on 3 October, 2012
judgments.holding: Service records, assets and disciplinary details of a public servant are 'personal information' exempt under Section 8(1)(j) unless a larger public interest is shown.
judgments.what_changed: The single most-cited refusal ground in India. Any RTI request touching an individual official's record will meet it, so requests must be framed around a system or a decision rather than a person.
judgments.status_note: Still applied, and heavily criticised for being read far more broadly than its facts warrant. Later benches have narrowed its use where public interest is demonstrated, so cite the public-interest proviso in any appeal.

judgments.case: Medha Kotwal Lele & Ors vs U.O.I. & Ors on 19 October, 2012
judgments.holding: Found the Vishaka guidelines widely unimplemented and issued directions to States and regulators to bring complaints mechanisms into being.
judgments.what_changed: Established that non-implementation is itself actionable — a complainant can go to the High Court where an employer has simply not constituted a committee.
judgments.status_note: Directions were largely absorbed into the POSH Act, 2013 and its Rules. The case remains the authority on what happens when the machinery exists only on paper.

judgments.case: Bachpan Bachao Andolan vs Union Of India & Ors on 18 April, 2011
judgments.holding: Directed action against trafficking of children into circuses and for their rescue and rehabilitation.
judgments.what_changed: Established rescue-plus-rehabilitation as the standard: removing a child without a rehabilitation plan is not compliance.

judgments.case: Nandini Sundar & Ors vs State Of Chattisgarh on 5 July, 2011
judgments.holding: Held the arming of civilians as Special Police Officers in counter-insurgency unconstitutional and directed disbanding of Salwa Judum.
judgments.what_changed: Central to conflict-affected programme work: the State cannot outsource force to irregulars, and the ruling names the harms that follow when it does.

judgments.case: Suchita Srivastava & Anr vs Chandigarh Administration on 28 August, 2009
judgments.holding: Reproductive choice is personal liberty under Article 21; pregnancy could not be terminated against the will of a woman with intellectual disability.
judgments.what_changed: Established that guardianship does not transfer reproductive decision-making, which is central to disability and institutional-care practice.

judgments.case: Anuj Garg & Ors vs Hotel Association Of India & Ors on 6 December, 2007
judgments.holding: Struck down a prohibition on women working in premises serving liquor as protective discrimination that failed strict scrutiny.
judgments.what_changed: The authority against 'for her own safety' restrictions on women's work — the State must fix the hazard, not exclude the worker.

judgments.case: Prakash Singh & Ors vs Union Of India And Ors on 22 September, 2006
judgments.holding: Issued seven binding directions on police reform, including fixed tenure, a State Security Commission, and separation of investigation from law and order.
judgments.what_changed: The reference point for every police-accountability argument in India, and a demonstration of how far court directions can go unimplemented.
judgments.status_note: Compliance across States has been partial and, by the Court's own later findings, frequently evaded through nominal legislation. Cite it for the standard, not for the state of affairs.

judgments.case: T.M.A.Pai Foundation & Ors vs State Of Karnataka & Ors on 31 October, 2002
judgments.holding: An eleven-judge bench held that private unaided institutions have autonomy in administration and admissions, subject to regulation against maladministration.
judgments.what_changed: The governing authority on private education. It is what displaced the Unni Krishnan scheme, and it sets the limits of state regulation over private schools and colleges.

judgments.case: Apparel Export Promotion Council vs A.K. Chopra on 20 January, 1999
judgments.holding: Sexual harassment does not require physical contact; conduct that outrages a woman's modesty and creates a hostile environment is enough to justify dismissal.
judgments.what_changed: Settled that an employer may act on non-contact conduct — advances, propositioning, sustained unwelcome attention — and that a disciplinary finding does not need the criminal standard of proof.

judgments.case: Samatha vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors on 11 July, 1997
judgments.holding: Transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals, including government leases to private mining companies, is void under the Fifth Schedule regime.
judgments.what_changed: The core authority against alienation of Adivasi land for extractive projects in Scheduled Areas.
judgments.status_note: Its reach has been contested and applied unevenly across States, and later benches have distinguished it on facts. Check the position in the specific State before relying on it.

judgments.case: Vishaka & Ors vs State Of Rajasthan & Ors on 13 August, 1997
judgments.holding: Absent a law on workplace sexual harassment, the Court framed binding guidelines under Article 32 and declared them enforceable until Parliament legislated.
judgments.what_changed: Gave every workplace a duty to constitute a complaints committee sixteen years before the POSH Act existed. Employers could no longer treat harassment as a private dispute between staff.
judgments.status_note: The Vishaka guidelines operated as binding law until the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 replaced them. Cite the Act for obligations; cite Vishaka for the reasoning the Act rests on.

judgments.case: Shri D.K. Basu,Ashok K. Johri vs State Of West Bengal,State Of U.P on 18 December, 1996
judgments.holding: Laid down mandatory safeguards for arrest and detention — memo of arrest, informing a relative, medical examination, and a record.
judgments.what_changed: The checklist used in every custodial-violence complaint, and the standard against which an arrest is judged procedurally invalid.
judgments.status_note: The safeguards were largely written into the Criminal Procedure Code (Sections 41A to 41D and 46) and carried into the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Cite the statute for the duty and D.K. Basu for its origin.

judgments.case: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulkpad vs Union Of India & Ors on 12 December, 1996
judgments.holding: Gave 'forest' its dictionary meaning regardless of ownership or classification, and placed forest governance under continuing court supervision.
judgments.what_changed: Extended forest protection to land never recorded as forest, and created the long-running supervisory jurisdiction that still governs diversion of forest land.
judgments.status_note: Runs as a continuing mandamus with hundreds of orders since 1996. Cite the specific order, not the case in the abstract.

judgments.case: M.C. Mehta vs State Of Tamil Nadu And Others on 10 December, 1996
judgments.holding: Directed elimination of child labour in hazardous industries with employer contributions to a welfare fund and compulsory education for the withdrawn child.
judgments.what_changed: Set the template of employer liability plus schooling that later child-labour policy is built on.

judgments.case: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoorsamity Of Ors vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 6 May, 1996
judgments.holding: Denial of emergency medical treatment by a government hospital violates Article 21; the State must provide adequate emergency facilities.
judgments.what_changed: Gives a patient refused emergency care a constitutional claim, and compensation, rather than only a grievance.

judgments.case: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum vs Union Of India & Ors on 28 August, 1996
judgments.holding: Adopted the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle as part of Indian environmental law.
judgments.what_changed: Reversed the burden: a project proponent must show an activity is safe, rather than an objector proving harm. Underpins most environmental regulation arguments since.

judgments.case: Chameli Singh vs State Of U.P on 15 December, 1995
judgments.holding: The right to shelter is part of the right to life, extending beyond a roof to civic amenities that make a dwelling liveable.
judgments.what_changed: Used to argue that resettlement sites without water, sanitation or access are not compliance with a rehabilitation obligation.

judgments.case: Unni Krishnan, J.P. And Ors. Etc. Etc vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. Etc. Etc on 4 February, 1993
judgments.holding: Recognised a fundamental right to free education up to age 14, and framed a scheme regulating private professional institutions.
judgments.what_changed: The direct ancestor of Article 21A and the RTE Act, 2009 — the reason elementary education is an entitlement rather than a service.
judgments.status_note: The scheme regulating private institutions was overruled by T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002). The right to elementary education survived and was constitutionalised as Article 21A. Do not cite the scheme; do cite the right.

judgments.case: Miss Mohini Jain vs State Of Karnataka And Ors on 30 July, 1992
judgments.holding: Charging capitation fees was unconstitutional; the right to education flows from the right to life.
judgments.what_changed: First recognised a constitutional right to education, opening the line that ends in Article 21A and the RTE Act.
judgments.status_note: Substantially reworked a year later in Unni Krishnan and again by T.M.A. Pai (2002) on private institutions. Cite it for the origin of the right, not for the current law on fees.

judgments.case: Subhash Kumar vs State Of Bihar And Ors on 9 January, 1991
judgments.holding: The right to life includes the right to enjoy pollution-free water and air.
judgments.what_changed: Made environmental quality a fundamental-rights claim, which is why environmental PILs are brought under Article 32 rather than only under statute.

judgments.case: M.C. Mehta And Anr vs Union Of India & Ors on 20 December, 1986
judgments.holding: Established absolute liability: an enterprise in a hazardous activity is liable for harm without exceptions, and the measure of damages scales with its capacity to pay.
judgments.what_changed: Went beyond the English rule in Rylands v. Fletcher by removing every defence. The basis of India's industrial-disaster liability, including later statutory public-liability insurance.

judgments.case: Olga Tellis & Ors vs Bombay Municipal Corporation & Ors. Etc on 10 July, 1985
judgments.holding: The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to livelihood; pavement dwellers could not be evicted without due process, though eviction itself was permitted.
judgments.what_changed: The foundation of every procedural-fairness argument in Indian eviction and resettlement work — notice, hearing, and the fact that losing a dwelling means losing a living.

judgments.case: Bandhua Mukti Morcha vs Union Of India & Others on 16 December, 1983
judgments.holding: Treated a letter as a writ petition, relaxed standing, and held that bonded labour is a violation of Article 21 requiring identification, release and rehabilitation.
judgments.what_changed: One of the cases that built public interest litigation itself, and the authority for demanding rehabilitation rather than mere release in bonded-labour work.

judgments.case: Francis Coralie Mullin vs The Administrator, Union Territory Of ... on 13 January, 1981
judgments.holding: Article 21 means more than animal existence: it includes living with human dignity and the bare necessities of life.
judgments.what_changed: The doctrinal root of the socio-economic rights line — nutrition, shelter and health arguments all trace back to this reading of Article 21.

judgments.case: Municipal Council, Ratlam vs Shri Vardhichand & Ors on 29 July, 1980
judgments.holding: A municipality cannot plead lack of funds to escape its statutory duty to provide sanitation and abate a public nuisance.
judgments.what_changed: The standing answer to 'no budget'. Used across sanitation, drainage and solid-waste litigation against local bodies.

judgments.case: Hussainara Khatoon & Ors vs Home Secretary, State Of Bihar, Govt. Of ... on 12 February, 1979
judgments.holding: Undertrials detained longer than the maximum sentence must be released; speedy trial and free legal aid are part of Article 21.
judgments.what_changed: The origin of legal-aid and undertrial-review work, and the authority behind statutory undertrial release provisions.
